summary: The psalms use חֶלֶד of a person’s lifetime and the world inhabited by people. Leviticus has a differently vocalized animal name with the same consonants.

senses.definition: A speaker measures his lifetime against the handbreadth of his days. Another asks God to remember how brief human life is.
The call to all inhabitants of the world opens Psalm 49. Psalm 17 describes people whose portion lies in their present life and whose goods pass to their children.
The animal heads a list of unclean creatures that move along the ground, immediately before the mouse. Arabic usage supports a burrowing mammal, though the verse gives no identifying description.

cognates.gloss: remain, abide for a long time

evidence.locator: خُلْدٌ, n11238, Book I, p. 784, animal sense A3

note: The Arabic parallels support both meanings independently. Neither the animal species nor a common origin for the duration and animal words can be determined from the biblical passages.
